message.content:
**Los Angeles → Berlin**

| Period | Los Angeles (PT) | Berlin (CET/CEST) | Δ（Berlin – LA） |
|--------|------------------|-------------------|------------------|
| **Standard time** (≈ Nov – Mar) | UTC‑08:00 | UTC+01:00 | **+9 h** |
| **Daylight‑saving time** (≈ Mar → Oct) | UTC‑07:00 | UTC+02:00 | **+9 h** |

> *In practice, Berlin is always nine hours ahead of Los Angeles.*  
> 
> This holds true today (May 18 2026), since both regions are observing Daylight Saving Time (PDT / CEST).

### Quick example  

If it’s **12:00 PM** noon in Los Angeles, it will be **9:00 PM** the same day in Berlin.  

---

#### When can the gap briefly change?

Because U.S. and EU switch DST on slightly different Sundays:

* **U.S. DST** starts on the **second Sunday in March**, ends on the **first Sunday in November**.  
* **EU/DACH DST** starts on the **last Sunday in March**, ends on the **last Sunday in October**.

During those few weeks around late March and early November, the two cities may momentarily have an **8‑hour** or **10‑hour** difference while only one side has switched its clocks. Outside those windows, the difference stays constant at 9 hours.
